new_page.title: Rosemary Heights South Surrey Homes and Neighbourhood Guide
new_page.description: Rosemary Heights in South Surrey: what homes near the school sold for, the condos, townhomes and 55+ homes, schools, parks and Jared’s tips.

blocks.text: Draft for Jared’s approval. Written November 10, 2026 from City of Surrey, Surrey School District and MLS® sources listed on the page.

Rosemary Heights is the planned neighbourhood on the east side of Highway 99 in South Surrey, between the Nicomekl River to the north and Titman Creek to the south, with the Morgan Creek golf course on its east side. The City laid it out in the 1990s: a local area plan in 1994, then neighbourhood plans for Rosemary Heights Central (1996), Rosemary Heights West (1997) and the Rosemary Heights Business Park (2000). The City now calls all three areas largely built out, so almost every home that comes up for sale here is a resale.

You will not find Rosemary Heights as an area on MLS®. The board files its listings under Morgan Creek, the sub-area named after the golf course community next door, which is why searches and market reports blend the two. This guide looks at Rosemary Heights on its own: the condo buildings along 36 Avenue and at Harvard Gardens, the 55+ community on Rosemary Heights Crescent, and the family streets around Rosemary Heights Elementary.

blocks.text: What homes near Rosemary Heights Elementary sold for

The board publishes nothing for Rosemary Heights alone, so the closest local measure is a 1 km circle around its school, which sits in the middle of the neighbourhood at 15516 36 Avenue. In the twelve months to October 31, 2026, 139 homes sold inside that circle: 54 condos, 51 townhomes and 34 detached houses. 109 of those sales were in the Morgan Creek sub-area and 30 in the neighbouring Grandview sub-area to the south, which the circle reaches.

blocks.text: Detached houses near the school sold at a median of $1,840,000, a little under the $1,960,000 median for the whole Morgan Creek sub-area, which includes the larger golf-course estates. Townhomes ($790,000) and condos ($557,500) were close to the sub-area medians of $785,000 and $552,500. Houses took longest to sell, at 31 days at the median, and sold for 95.3% of the asking price.

Quarter by quarter, the median for all home types together went $780,000 (November to January), $850,000 (February to April), $732,500 (May to July) and $710,000 (August to October). Those figures mix condos and houses, so a quarter with more condo sales reads lower. Price a home from the by-type rows instead.
Condos, townhomes and 55+ homes in Rosemary Heights

The apartment buildings sit on the west side of the neighbourhood, in two groups. Along 36 Avenue west of 152 Street are Edgewater, a gated community at 15195 36 Avenue built in 2013 above the Nicomekl River, and Tehama, at 3355 Rosemary Heights Drive, built in 2008. Near 32 Avenue and 151 Street is Harvard Gardens, which includes Kingston House and Prescott Commons.

Within the 1 km circle, Edgewater had the most condo sales over the year (13, at a median of $678,000), followed by Headwaters (8, $578,500), Prescott Commons (5, $525,000) and Harvard Gardens (5, $555,000). On the townhome side, Sundance led with 8 sales at a median of $681,950.

parts.t: The 55+ homes you can buy are in the Carrington community on Rosemary Heights Crescent: The Carrington at 15500, Carrington at 15450 and Braemore at Carrington at 15425. Rosemary Heights Seniors Village, at 15240 34 Avenue, is a different kind of place: a seniors campus with independent living, assisted living and long-term care that you rent or are placed in, not a strata you buy into. blocks.text: The City lists two elementary schools for Rosemary Heights: Rosemary Heights Elementary (kindergarten to grade 7, 15516 36 Avenue) and Morgan Elementary (kindergarten to grade 7, 3366 156A Street), about half a kilometre apart. Addresses checked on Rosemary Heights Crescent and Morgan Creek Way were in the Grandview Heights Secondary catchment (16987 25 Avenue) for grades 8 to 12. The nearest independent school is Southridge School, kindergarten to grade 12, at 2656 160 Street, about 2 km away.

items.t: Rosemary Heights Park, 3501 154 Street: wide lawns and paths laid out like a traditional British common, with a picnic area. Its paths carry on east through Blumsen Park.

Blumsen Park, 15473 34 Avenue: a playground and a large wooded area with forest trails, between Rosemary Heights Drive and 34 Avenue, just south of Rosemary Heights Elementary. It is named after Blumsen Avenue, the old name for 34 Avenue.

Nicomekl Riverfront Park: a 3 km, 80-acre linear park the City is building along the south bank of the Nicomekl River, from Elgin Road to 40 Avenue. Most of it is still being designed and is closed. The fenced Nicomekl Dog Off-Leash Park, about an acre at 3435 150 Street, is open and is reached on foot from the pathway, with no parking.
Morgan Creek Park, 3302 156A Street, on the golf-course side.
Route 354 (TransLink) runs between White Rock South and Bridgeport Station on the Canada Line, via 32 Avenue and 160 Street.
Route 363 runs from Peace Arch Hospital to King George Boulevard at 32 Avenue, via 160 Street and 24 Avenue.
Highway 99 runs along the west edge of the neighbourhood. Morgan Crossing and Grandview Corners, the main shopping areas, are a short drive south-east.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Rosemary Heights

items.t: Walk the street at school drop-off or pickup. The streets beside Rosemary Heights Elementary and Blumsen Park are busy for half an hour twice a day, and a block or two away they are quiet.

Look at what is behind the lot. The City notes a river, fish-bearing creeks and rare wetland habitat in Rosemary Heights, and a home that backs onto a creek or the Nicomekl can have setbacks that limit fences, decks and additions. Ask the City before you plan a project.
If the home is close to Highway 99, go back at rush hour to hear it.
For a townhome or condo, read the strata minutes, Form B and depreciation report before you remove subjects, and compare fees by strata plan, since some complexes share a name across several plans.

The Rosemary Heights neighbourhood plans were rescinded when the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan came in, so a rezoning nearby is now judged against the OCP. Check for development applications near the address.

faq.q: Is Rosemary Heights part of Morgan Creek?
faq.a: On MLS®, yes: the board files Rosemary Heights listings under the Morgan Creek sub-area. The City of Surrey treats Rosemary Heights as its own planned neighbourhood, west of the Morgan Creek golf course.

faq.q: Where are the edges of Rosemary Heights?
faq.a: The City describes Rosemary Heights as south of the Nicomekl River, east of Highway 99 and north of Titman Creek, with the golf course on its east side.

faq.q: Are new homes being built in Rosemary Heights?
faq.a: Very few. The City calls the neighbourhood largely built out, so most homes for sale are resales. Newer townhomes and condos nearby are mostly in Grandview Heights, to the south-east.

faq.q: Is Rosemary Heights Seniors Village a 55+ strata?
faq.a: No. It is a seniors campus with independent living, assisted living and long-term care that you rent or are placed in. The 55+ homes you can buy are in the Carrington community on Rosemary Heights Crescent.
